scores.label: Scoped WSG audit score
scores.formula: 100 * passed / (passed + failed + cantTell), grouped once per guideline

impactWeighted.status: Experimental project convention using WSG impact priority points; not a W3C site score

scores.interpretation: Passes satisfy only the declared scoped expectations; unknowns earn no points but are not defects. Compare only matching rubric, sample, and evidence profiles.

guidelines.title: Identify, assess, disclose, review, and mitigate sustainability impacts
guidelines.expectation: A retrieved public sustainability statement identifies the audited service and describes its impacts and mitigation. Judge disclosure only, not execution; an unresolved relationship is cantTell.

judgments.rationale: The retrieved sustainability listing and Stegra announcement describe Google products, operations, partnerships and construction materials. They do not identify blog.google resource use or mitigation. Their existence is corporate context, not this web publication's service disclosure; lack of a matching statement in the bounded search is not proof none exists.
judgments.nextEvidence: Supply a public statement identifying this publication and its environmental impacts and mitigation.

guidelines.title: Understand user requirements or constraints
Integrate sustainability into every stage of the ideation process
Design efficient and streamlined user journeys
guidelines.expectation: Execute declared task actions and inspect completion evidence; an expected selector is one observable, not proof of user success or optimal journey length.

judgments.rationale: The declared listing-to-Stegra journey acknowledges the cookie notice, opens the featured article and reaches its canonical URL, full headline and readable main body. Captured postconditions and the independent walkthrough support completion without login; they do not establish optimum journey length.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Design to assist and not to distract
guidelines.expectation: Assess visible distractions against the declared visitor task; distinguish useful prompts from interruptions.

judgments.rationale: The six page samples retain their headings and main tasks, and the article/newsletter prompts are identifiable. The homepage contains multiple simultaneously playing muted videos and a rotating feature area while readers browse; pause controls are exposed, but their effectiveness and the visibility of moving content throughout the task are not exercised. A reading interruption is plausible but not established by isolated snapshots.
judgments.nextEvidence: Observe the homepage browsing task with moving tiles and activate its pause controls; assess whether movement competes with choosing a story.

guidelines.title: Avoid being manipulative or deceptive
guidelines.expectation: Inspect choice wording, defaults, prominence and the observed accept/reject paths for undue steering. DOM text alone does not establish visual parity.

judgments.rationale: The cookie banner says OK, got it and links to further information. The captured task correctly treats this as notice acknowledgement, not a tested accept/reject consent pair. Newsletter signup is optional and its opt-out wording is clear. No visual prominence, consent default comparison or rejection route is established, so neither manipulation nor fair consent parity is proven.
judgments.nextEvidence: Inspect the linked cookie controls and actual choice behavior in the represented context, with screenshots if judging visual steering.

guidelines.title: Make deliverables understandable and reusable
guidelines.expectation: Assess the sampled task's wording, headings and terminology for its stated audience; retain uncertainty about unrepresented users.

judgments.rationale: All six pages have identifiable topic, article, newsletter or about headings with plain task labels. The Stegra announcement identifies authors, date and a short main body; its EAC explanation distinguishes the purchasing arrangement from manufacturing itself. Newsletter wording describes weekly updates and opt-out. This judgment covers sampled English wording, not independent verification of corporate claims.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Use a design system for interface consistency
guidelines.expectation: Compare repeated navigation and control names across sampled pages; consistent samples do not prove a documented design system.

judgments.rationale: Repeated Innovation & AI, Products & platforms, Company news, Feed and Newsletter navigation, Search title and region controls retain their names across the six templates. Article topic breadcrumbs and follow/share controls recur consistently. No documented design system is inferred.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Optimize media to reduce resource use
guidelines.expectation: The sampled task images preserve useful content and provide proportionate intrinsic dimensions and delivery choices for their rendered size and pixel density. A large image is an investigation candidate until legibility and task value are checked; absent srcset alone is not a failure.

judgments.rationale: The sample mixes responsive WebP cards and lazy loading with oversized homepage assets and undersized author headshots (100 pixels displayed at 240). A Stegra related-story image is 2784 pixels at roughly 283 rendered pixels. These are useful rendition candidates, but no visual inspection at intended density establishes acceptable detail or a task-affecting quality defect; absent srcset alone does not fail.
judgments.nextEvidence: Inspect the cited large card and headshot renditions at intended pixel densities, then choose dimensions that preserve editorial image detail.

guidelines.title: Ensure animation is proportionate and easy to control
guidelines.expectation: Assess observed animation purpose, playback controls and reduced-motion behavior. A quiet snapshot does not prove no motion occurs elsewhere.

judgments.rationale: Two visible homepage videos continue playing after the in-page reduced-motion change, despite being paused in the cold reduced-motion/dark observation. Several one-iteration transitions also remain, but their purpose and effect are not diagnosed. Named pause controls are present, so this finding concerns the demonstrated preference-change response, not a claim that playback is impossible to control.
judgments.nextEvidence: Pause active autoplay tiles when reduced motion becomes active, and verify manual replay and pause still work.

guidelines.title: Use optimized web typography
guidelines.expectation: Observed web fonts and variants serve the sampled content, with a declared fallback/loading strategy where needed. Do not fail a site merely for using a web font; recommend removal or subsetting only after language and readability requirements are established.

judgments.rationale: Observed loaded Google Sans regular/medium faces serve sampled body and heading text with font-display:swap and Roboto/Arial/Helvetica fallbacks. Numerous declared language-range faces are unloaded; declarations are not downloads. The evidence supports a fallback/loading strategy without establishing unused-language removal or every possible state.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Avoid unwanted notifications
guidelines.expectation: Assess observed alerts and notification permission requests for user value and choice; absence is limited to observed states.

judgments.rationale: No notification permission calls are recorded on any of the six pages. Newsletter entry is offered as an explicit user choice with opt-out text; the captured page states show no unsolicited notification dialog. Browser permission was already denied and no subscription was submitted, limiting this pass to observed states.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Reduce the impact of downloadable and physical documents
guidelines.expectation: Review print layout visibility and download labels for the declared task. Fetch and inspect document content before asserting optimization or equivalence.

judgments.rationale: Article and about pages load a print stylesheet and preserve headings and main text in print emulation. The homepage still has horizontal overflow and several templates retain navigation. No physical pagination or document-content inspection establishes an efficient full-sample print route; download presence alone would not establish optimization.
judgments.nextEvidence: Inspect printed output for the homepage and article templates, including overflow/page breaks; inspect any task-relevant downloadable document before judging equivalence.

guidelines.title: Involve users early in the project
Audit and test for bugs or issues requiring resolution
Validate usability through testing and real-world usage
Provide cross-platform compatibility support
guidelines.expectation: The sampled core reading content and navigation remain available without JavaScript, or an explicit alternative supports the task. This bounded check does not establish no-JavaScript search, every interaction, or all browser compatibility.

judgments.rationale: The Stegra article, Fitbit reading text, newsletter explanation and about page retain core text without JavaScript. However the sustainability listing loses the featured article and latest story links entirely, and the homepage loses most feed content. No explicit alternative route for that core collection discovery task is captured. This fails the full declared page sample, without requiring no-JavaScript search or playback.
judgments.nextEvidence: Render core topic/story links in HTML or provide a discoverable lightweight index available without scripts.

guidelines.title: Set goals based on performance and energy impact
Minify and remove unused code
guidelines.expectation: Use initial JS/CSS execution observations to nominate investigation targets; require representative journeys or source corroboration before recommending removal.

judgments.rationale: Initial coverage is bounded to 500 ms and function/range samples are truncated. It can nominate the common bundle, page chunks and carousel/player code for investigation, but search, menu, feed expansion, playback and signup are not comprehensively exercised. No safe code deletion follows from unexecuted ranges.
judgments.nextEvidence: Collect representative journey coverage and identify concrete modules before recommending removal.

guidelines.title: Modularize bandwidth-heavy components
guidelines.expectation: Relate initial script resources to visible components and later task needs; recommend splitting only when a component's deferred use and usable activation are corroborated.

judgments.rationale: The network already shows separate CSS/JS chunks. Homepage media, article audio and newsletter widgets are identifiable later-use components, but the packet does not correlate each module with activation or test an on-demand replacement. Additional splitting could introduce overhead and is not justified merely by script count.
judgments.nextEvidence: Trace component initiators and activation for one expensive optional feature; compare existing chunks before proposing further splitting.

guidelines.title: Avoid redundancy and duplication in code
Treat third parties the same as first parties
Ensure code follows good semantic practices
guidelines.expectation: The sampled document has a meaningful language, primary heading and main region, and task controls have visible labels or an explicit naming relationship. Count/attribute presence alone does not establish semantic correctness or WCAG compliance. The sampled initial keyboard path reaches visible task navigation/controls in a meaningful order with a discernible focus indicator. A bounded Tab trace cannot establish complete keyboard support, reverse navigation, traps or screen-reader accessibility.

judgments.rationale: All six pages have en-us, a main region and meaningful task headings. The homepage uses several feature H1s, which is not automatically a failure of this narrow check. Search has a Search title; menu, media, region and newsletter controls have text/title/ARIA names, including the labeled required email field. This is not a WCAG or complete accessible-name audit.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

judgments.rationale: The initial Tab traces reach meaningful cookie, skip, logo and navigation controls; skip and logo have solid blue outlines. The first cookie link/button outlines are transparent and other focus styling was not captured. Their discernible indicator is unresolved, not a demonstrated invisible focus defect.
judgments.nextEvidence: Capture the focused cookie controls and remaining initial controls to establish visible background, border or shadow changes.

guidelines.title: Defer the loading of non-critical resources
Structure metadata for machine readability
guidelines.expectation: The sampled content has a descriptive title and usable canonical metadata when applicable; declared structured-data blocks parse as JSON. Judge description and other optional metadata according to page purpose, not a mandatory-field checklist.

judgments.rationale: All six pages have task-descriptive titles and matching absolute canonicals. Declared JSON-LD parses, including NewsArticle/WebSite/AboutPage. Newsletter has a sufficient title/canonical for its simple signup purpose; a missing optional description is not failed. Schema validity and eligibility remain outside scope.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Use media queries that support sustainability goals
guidelines.expectation: The sampled page respects applicable dark/reduced-motion preferences both before navigation and when they change in-page, without losing task content. Distinguish intentional design choices and absence of applicable motion from unsupported behavior.

judgments.rationale: In-page reduced motion pauses one homepage video but leaves two visible autoplay videos running; cold navigation with the preference active leaves them paused. This directly distinguishes incomplete live preference handling from initialization. Light colors alone do not establish a theme defect, and task text remains available.
judgments.nextEvidence: Apply the same reduced-motion media logic on a live change as on initial navigation, and verify all visible autoplay tiles stop.

guidelines.title: Ensure layouts work for different devices and requirements
guidelines.expectation: Compare narrow and desktop task content and overflow, then exercise affected controls; width emulation alone is not real-device compatibility.

judgments.rationale: Five page templates show no desktop/narrow overflow and retain task text. The homepage records a 2368-pixel document in a 1280-pixel viewport, while narrow emulation removes that overflow. Its carousel/offscreen content may explain the measurement; no screenshot or affected navigation activation establishes a clipped task or safe operation. Narrow menu behavior is also unexercised.
judgments.nextEvidence: Inspect homepage horizontal scroll and feature controls, then complete navigation through the narrow menu.

guidelines.title: Use sustainable JavaScript and APIs
guidelines.expectation: Repeated observed API requests are justified by the sampled task and its update needs. Identify redundant-looking requests for investigation without inferring backend cost or safe removal from URL repetition alone.

judgments.rationale: Page states include analytics and dynamically loaded article collections. The bounded record does not establish whether repeated endpoints are redundant requests, pagination or required update events, and it omits backend cost. Successful article navigation cannot justify every background call.
judgments.nextEvidence: Trace the homepage and topic collection requests by initiator and update event; identify any repeat with unchanged parameters and no task need before changing it.

guidelines.title: Use dependencies sparingly and maintain them
Include expected and beneficial files
guidelines.expectation: The sampled service exposes a discoverable, parseable carbon.txt with usable declared relationships. Missing carbon.txt is a scoped absence, not proof of high emissions or failure of the entire guideline. Judge redirects, delegation, supported versions and schema findings explicitly.

judgments.rationale: The root and well-known carbon.txt attempts return 404, and no usable header/DNS delegation or parsed document is established. There is no supported version/schema to judge. This is scoped absence of carbon.txt, not evidence of high publication emissions.
judgments.nextEvidence: Publish a discoverable parseable carbon.txt only with useful verifiable relationships.

guidelines.title: Use the most efficient solution for your service
Use the latest stable language version
Reduce the number and complexity of database queries
Use sustainable hosting
guidelines.expectation: Hosting claims identify provider, service and supporting evidence with a relationship to this origin. Self-declaration without independently corroborated operational scope remains cantTell for sustainable hosting; do not set SWDM green-hosting flags from this check.

judgments.rationale: Google Cloud/storage and corporate energy statements cannot alone identify the operational hosting boundary and independently corroborate sustainable hosting for this origin. The discovery supplies no such chain of evidence.
judgments.nextEvidence: Link the audited origin to its hosting service and provide independently corroborated operational evidence; do not infer a green-hosting model flag.

guidelines.title: Optimize caching and support offline access
guidelines.expectation: Reusable public scripts/styles/media expose an appropriate caching or validation policy in the sample. Distinguish dynamic/private responses and note that headers alone do not prove cache reuse or offline support.

judgments.rationale: Reusable versioned publication scripts/styles have long public cache lifetimes. Font styles and external helpers expose shorter private lifetimes; media responses have validators/lifetimes. This supports reusable public-resource policy, while HTML and analytics responses have different purposes. Neither warm-load reuse nor offline support was tested.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Reduce data transfer with compression
guidelines.expectation: Material sampled text assets are delivered with compression where beneficial. Do not demand compression for already-compressed images, tiny bodies or error responses without context.

judgments.rationale: The sampled successful material HTML, scripts, styles and JSON/text responses use gzip or Brotli. No material successful text response without content-encoding appears in the six bounded network records. This does not demand further compression of video, WebP or fonts.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Setup necessary error pages and redirection links
Avoid maintaining unnecessary virtualized environments or containers
Use automation wisely
Define the frequency of data refreshes
Back up critical data at routine intervals
Assess the impact and requirements of data processing
Use Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) when beneficial
Ensure infrastructure fits project requirements
Store data according to the needs of your users
Have an ethical and sustainable product strategy
Assign a sustainability advocate
Inform, raise awareness, and train for sustainability
Communicate the environmental impact of user choices
guidelines.expectation: Identify consequential user choices in the sample and assess whether contextual impact information is useful and supported. Do not prescribe carbon labels on every control.

judgments.rationale: The Stegra article offers reading and optional audio, and the Fitbit page offers a selected video. The homepage autoplays some media. These are more consequential than routine link clicks, but no measured data comparison, effective disable-all choice or tested transcript alternative establishes appropriate impact guidance. Corporate steel claims are unrelated to the impact of reading this publication.
judgments.nextEvidence: Test media alternatives and measure their relative transfer before offering contextual data-use information.

guidelines.title: Calculate the environmental impact
Define clear organizational sustainability goals and metrics
guidelines.expectation: Published goals for the audited web service define a measurable target or direction, relevant metric and boundary, and communicate dated progress against a comparable baseline. A corporate net-zero ambition or isolated low-carbon badge cannot establish service-specific goals and progress.

judgments.assessmentScope: News from Google web publication at https://blog.google, as publicly described on 2026-11-06: assess web-service-specific measurable sustainability goals and dated comparable progress. The sustainability topic listing and selected Stegra article are corporate context only and cannot establish the publication’s own goals or operational results.
judgments.rationale: The Stegra estimates and construction-project examples concern corporate materials procurement, while the about page describes the publication. None supplies a web-publication metric, baseline, target and comparable progress for blog.google. Missing evidence is an unknown rather than a failed corporate target.
judgments.nextEvidence: Provide a publication-specific resource/impact goal, measurement boundary and comparable dated baseline and progress.

guidelines.title: Validate web sustainability efforts through external verification
Support mandatory disclosures and reporting
Create one or more impact business models
Follow a product management and maintenance strategy
Implement continuous improvement procedures
Document updates and evolutions
Evaluate if a digital product or service is necessary
guidelines.expectation: For the declared visitor task and represented access constraints, inspect material accessibility, technical, geographic or fairness barriers and verify the sampled route or alternative supports task completion while preserving necessary security and safety. Do not demand removal of justified authentication or infer all-user accessibility from one successful route.

judgments.assessmentScope: Anonymous English-language desktop readers (1440×1000, pointer and ordinary browser, no account): from the sustainability topic listing, acknowledge the visible cookie notice and open the featured Stegra article; completion requires the canonical article URL, its complete headline and readable main article content. Keyboard-only, constrained-device and geographic completion are not represented.
judgments.rationale: The anonymous English desktop pointer journey from sustainability listing to Stegra completes after acknowledging the notice, without account or personal-data entry. The canonical article, complete headline and main body are captured. No material barrier blocks this exact represented task; keyboard, geography and constrained-device success are excluded by the frozen scope.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

guidelines.title: Provide a supplier standards of practice document
Share economic benefits
Share decision-making power with affected parties
Use Diversity, Equity, Justice, Inclusion (DEJI) practices
Promote responsible data practices
guidelines.expectation: For the sampled data-collecting task, each requested personal-data category has a task-related purpose, required and optional choices are meaningful, and observed controls match the stated purpose. A privacy policy cannot establish actual retention, downstream deletion or all-system consent propagation; keep those outside this bounded task judgment. For a declared content collection, evidence identifies a review/expiry schedule and demonstrates an applied archive, update or deletion decision, with a lightweight discoverable historical version where users still need it. A date label, old article or policy alone cannot establish an effective lifecycle or justify deletion.

judgments.assessmentScope: The public News from Google newsletter sign-up task at /newsletter-subscribe/ as observed on 2026-11-06: inspect visible requested personal-data categories, mandatory/optional states, purpose and opt-out explanation before entering data or submitting. Retention, downstream deletion and all-system propagation are outside this boundary.
judgments.rationale: The signup asks only for a required email address, explicitly to receive weekly Google news/stories, and explains opt-out before entry. That category is necessary for the chosen email delivery task; no account, name or other personal fields are requested in this observation. The linked broad privacy excerpt supports email-updates purpose without proving blog-specific downstream processing. No submission, retention or deletion behavior is inferred.
judgments.nextEvidence: No further evidence is needed for this bounded expectation; recheck after relevant changes.

judgments.assessmentScope: The English News from Google sustainability article collection, represented by its topic listing, the September 17, 2026 Stegra article and publication about page as available on 2026-11-06: assess public review/expiry scheduling and an applied update/archive/deletion example with useful historical access. No CMS history or organization-wide lifecycle is represented.
judgments.rationale: The sampled article date, author attribution, historical publication description and current listing establish useful published news content. They do not identify a review/expiry schedule or an executed update/archive/deletion decision for this collection. Historical announcements can retain research value, so age is not a removal defect.
judgments.nextEvidence: Supply one collection-specific review schedule and dated applied decision, with historical access where readers need it.

guidelines.title: Establish responsible practices around AI and emerging or disruptive technologies
Adopt responsible financial practices
Adopt organizational philanthropy practices
Plan for a digital product or service's care and end-of-life
Repair, reuse, refurbish, recycle or reduce e-waste
Define performance, environmental, and human budgets
Use and contribute to open source
Create a business continuity and disaster recovery plan
